purpose: Canonical extension modules for Weeks 16-20 of the Electrical Career Readiness Hub.

learn.objective: Develop a disciplined workflow for arranging switchboards and MCCs with equipment interfaces, cable entry, maintainability and documentation traceability.
learn.seniorReasoning: A senior layout balances electrical function, installation, maintenance and document consistency rather than optimizing only for physical fit.

apply.scenario: Develop a fictional MCC arrangement serving several motor feeders, a control section and incoming supply.
tasks: Establish incomer, bus-section and outgoing arrangement logic.
Reserve space for terminals, cable entry and future capacity where required.
Identify access and maintenance constraints.
Cross-check equipment tags and feeder references against a fictional SLD.
Record vendor and engineer inputs that must be confirmed before issue.
apply.deliverable: Sanitized MCC/switchboard GA sketch with layout checklist, assumptions and discrepancy record.

questions.prompt: The MCC physically fits but cable termination access is poor. What is the strongest response?
questions.answer: Treat termination access and maintainability as design constraints and revise the arrangement before issue.

questions.prompt: What should be coordinated when an MCC feeder is added?
questions.answer: The GA, SLD, cable schedule, protection information, interfaces and revision/change records.

questions.prompt: When should a layout assumption be escalated?
questions.answer: When it affects safety, equipment interface, maintainability, compliance or a vendor/engineer approval boundary.

evidence.prompt: Capture a sanitized switchboard or MCC layout exercise demonstrating coordinated arrangement and design ownership.

learn.objective: Coordinate electrical drawings with instrumentation and control interfaces so field devices, panels, signals and interfaces remain traceable.
learn.seniorReasoning: Senior coordination makes interfaces explicit: who owns the signal, where it terminates, what power or communication dependency exists and what remains to be confirmed.

apply.scenario: Coordinate a fictional pump control system containing level instruments, motor status, run commands, alarms and a PLC interface.
tasks: Create a signal/interface register.
Map field devices to panel/PLC termination points.
Separate power, discrete, analogue and communication interfaces.
Identify three missing or conflicting inputs.
Prepare a multidisciplinary coordination checklist.
apply.deliverable: Sanitized I/O/interface register with a simplified termination/loop mapping and discrepancy record.

questions.prompt: A field instrument tag exists in the P&ID but not in the electrical I/O list. What is the strongest response?
questions.answer: Record the interface discrepancy, trace the controlled source and coordinate the intended signal before finalizing electrical documentation.

questions.prompt: Why separate power and signal interfaces?
questions.answer: They have different design, segregation, termination and verification considerations and must remain traceable.

questions.prompt: What should be confirmed before assigning a PLC termination?
questions.answer: Signal type, source, destination, I/O ownership, termination arrangement and approved control philosophy.

evidence.prompt: Capture a sanitized control-interface register or loop/termination exercise showing traceability across disciplines.

learn.objective: Build a reviewable workflow for electrical load, cable and voltage-drop calculations using controlled inputs and documented assumptions.
learn.seniorReasoning: The senior skill is not memorizing a table; it is knowing which inputs drive the result, documenting them and recognizing when engineering verification is required.

apply.scenario: Prepare a fictional feeder-sizing worksheet for a pump motor and auxiliary loads using supplied design inputs and intentionally incomplete installation information.
tasks: Create an input register for load, length, installation method and environmental conditions.
Show the calculation workflow and identify required standard references.
Perform a voltage-drop check using clearly stated assumptions.
Identify which inputs would change the selected cable/protection.
Flag results requiring engineer verification.
apply.deliverable: Sanitized calculation worksheet or design-note exercise with assumptions, checks and escalation points.

questions.prompt: The cable length is uncertain and voltage drop is close to the project limit. What is the strongest response?
questions.answer: Do not hide the uncertainty; confirm the route/length, document the assumption and reassess the calculation before final selection.

questions.prompt: Which inputs should be traceable in a cable-sizing calculation?
questions.answer: Load/current, cable length, installation method, correction factors/conditions, allowable voltage drop and applicable design assumptions.

questions.prompt: When should a calculation be escalated?
questions.answer: When inputs are incomplete, the result is marginal, or the design decision requires engineering judgement or approval.

evidence.prompt: Capture a sanitized load/cable-sizing worksheet demonstrating traceable inputs, calculation logic and engineering escalation awareness.

learn.objective: Perform a structured electrical design check that tests technical content, interfaces, standards, revisions and issue readiness.
learn.seniorReasoning: A strong checker looks for consequences and omissions, not only drafting errors, and writes comments that allow the designer to resolve them efficiently.

apply.scenario: Review a fictional electrical package containing an SLD, board GA, cable schedule and control interface sheet with deliberate inconsistencies.
tasks: Create a checking plan before reviewing.
Identify technical, coordination, drafting and document-control issues.
Classify comments by severity and required action.
Trace each major comment to affected documents.
Prepare a closure recommendation and unresolved-risk statement.
apply.deliverable: Sanitized design-check register with classified comments, cross-document impacts and closure status.

questions.prompt: A drawing looks correct but a cable schedule contradicts it. How should the checker respond?
questions.answer: Raise the traceability issue, identify the affected documents and require resolution before issue.

questions.prompt: What distinguishes an effective checking comment?
questions.answer: It identifies the issue, consequence or required clarification clearly enough for the designer to act.

questions.prompt: When is a package not ready for closure?
questions.answer: When significant technical, safety, compliance, interface or traceability issues remain unresolved or evidence of resolution is inadequate.

evidence.prompt: Capture a sanitized design-check register demonstrating structured QA reasoning and comment closure discipline.

learn.objective: Control redlines and revisions so changes are traceable, correctly incorporated and reflected consistently across the drawing package.
learn.seniorReasoning: Revision control is a risk-control activity: every change needs an understood source, impact, disposition and verification path.

apply.scenario: Process a fictional redline package containing equipment relocation, feeder changes and annotation corrections across four related drawings.
tasks: Classify each markup by change type.
Identify affected drawings and schedules.
Record clarification questions before editing.
Prepare revision descriptions and a disposition log.
Perform a post-incorporation package check.
apply.deliverable: Sanitized redline disposition register, revision record and post-update QA checklist.

questions.prompt: A redline is unclear but could affect cable routing. What is the strongest response?
questions.answer: Raise a clarification before incorporating the change and record the potential downstream impact.

questions.prompt: Why assess change impact before editing?
questions.answer: Because one markup can affect multiple drawings, schedules, references and design assumptions.
The change is incorporated, affected documents are checked, revision information is updated and unresolved items are recorded.

evidence.prompt: Capture a sanitized redline/revision exercise demonstrating controlled change incorporation and verification.
